A1.justification: The PDFs describe the same Pythia/SAE study despite the changed title. Their main text, equations, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original SAE experiments on trained and randomized Pythia models, feature analyses, and toy-model and embedding experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds detection scoring, training-budget and hyperparameter experiments, seed-based uncertainty plots, and feature-level analyses.

M1.justification: The TopK SAE procedure, transformer randomization constructions, and ReLU/L1 toy autoencoders remain unchanged. Additional scoring procedures and hyperparameter experiments do not introduce a new SAE algorithm or architecture.

E1.justification: v2 actually evaluates detection classification alongside fuzzing: the evaluator identifies examples containing activating tokens, rather than judging marked tokens (Section 3 and Appendix B). The underlying RedPajama, Pythia, GloVe and synthetic-data coverage is retained.

E2.justification: The evaluated transformer comparisons retain Trained, Step-0, re-randomized variants including/excluding embeddings, and the inconsistent Gaussian-embedding Control. Toy experiments retain Gaussian-input controls; newly discussed prior methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The default 100M-token, R=64, k=32 setup remains, but substantial additional protocols are evaluated. These include 1B-token training for Pythia-70M/410M, 1M- and 1B-token training for Pythia-1B, R=2 with k=4 or 256, and detection scoring (Appendices B–D and G).

E4.justification: v2 retains the earlier Pythia-160M sweep and toy analyses, while adding tests of training-data sufficiency, severe undertraining and extreme SAE capacity/sparsity settings. Appendix H adds per-latent entropy-versus-interpretability analysis, and Appendix L adds 80 detailed feature dashboards beyond the retained examples.

E5.justification: v2 adds uncertainty plots over five random seeds for Pythia-70M (Appendix E), extending uncertainty reporting beyond v1's toy experiments. The toy study's ten-seed count remains, but v1 Figure 6's explicit SEM description is omitted from v2 Figure 5; the new transformer error-bar statistic is also unspecified.

E6.justification: v2 adds detection results across the Pythia sizes and substantial results from the new budget, hyperparameter and feature analyses. Figure 19 shows that reduced reconstruction quality can coexist with similar auto-interpretability scores; Figure 20 reveals high-entropy, high-scoring latents in trained models. These extend v1's evidence rather than establish a same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: The Lomax/Gaussian construction, linear-transformation argument for preserving superposition, and synthetic-data generation mathematics are retained. Moving displayed equations inline and relocating Appendix C to Appendix I do not change the mathematical substance.

C1.justification: v1 emphasizes similarly interpretable latents and suggests SAEs provide limited insight into learned computation. v2 substantially narrows the central claim to the insufficiency of aggregate evaluation metrics, qualifies similarity as occurring under certain conditions, and explicitly allows trained-model SAEs to recover meaningful computational features.

C2.justification: v2 adds the interpretation that SAEs may faithfully describe simple computation in random networks and explains how aggregate scores obscure feature-level differences (Introduction and Appendix H). Its new Limitations section identifies dependence on Pythia, RedPajama-V2 and one explanation model, while explicitly limiting conclusions about SAE capabilities.

D1.justification: Appendix K newly discloses use of a single NVIDIA A100 80GB GPU and approximate runtimes by model and variant, totaling 435 hours for final experiments, with preliminary/failed experiments estimated to cost roughly as much. Existing toy implementation and training details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds focused positioning against Karvonen et al.'s board-game findings and Bricken et al.'s random one-layer transformer results, plus Adebayo et al.'s randomization sanity checks and several newer references. Most of the earlier related-work framework remains.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, substantial introductory passages and conclusion are rewritten around evaluation-metric validity. Results subsections become paragraph headings, a dedicated Limitations section is introduced, and the appendices are reorganized into a more extensive topical structure.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, ROC plots are redrawn with numerical AUC legends, and the summary figure gains a detection row. The 410M ROC display moves to the appendix, the main Pareto figures are merged, and new analysis plots, a compute table and activation-colored dashboards are added.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially improves claim calibration and empirical support. It replaces v1's broader implications about SAE limitations with a more defensible conclusion about aggregate metrics, supported by training-budget and capacity controls, detection evaluation and feature-level analysis. Explicit limitations and compute disclosure further improve assessability. Uncertainty reporting remains incompletely specified, but the gains address important weaknesses in the earlier argument.
